PLAN YOUR REQUIREMENT

A useful brief.
A clearer next step.

Mechanical subassemblies, complete products and assemblies combining mechanical and electrical elements.

Decisions to make early

A clear bill of materials and assembly sequence help identify missing parts and access issues. Include fastening, cable routing, adjustment and functional test requirements.

What to agree before work begins

Agree component responsibilities, assembly revision, inspection and test steps, labelling and packaging requirements.

BEFORE YOU ENQUIRE

Questions,
answered.

What should I prepare for an assembly enquiry?+

Provide the bill of materials, assembly drawings, component supply plan and quantity. Include work instructions or a reference sample if available, plus the checks required before dispatch.

Should packaging be considered during assembly planning?+

Yes. Share the delivery route, protection needs and whether the product will travel fully assembled or in sections. Packing and any installation requirements should be agreed with the scope.

A CLEAR START

What to share.

Bill of materials, assembly drawings, test requirements and packaging needs.

Technical scope, material suitability, tolerances, inspection criteria, pricing and timing are confirmed after reviewing your requirements.
